mainTopic: The dangers of speech, the seven sins that bring נגעים, and what atones for murder and לשון הרע
overview: This amud continues the discussion of good and bad speech. רבה בר רב הונא rules that something said in front of three people may be repeated, because it will spread anyway. רב דימי explains that loudly praising a generous host can bring him trouble, and a teaching warns that praising someone leads to talking about his faults. רבי יוחנן then lists seven sins that bring נגעים, and the גמרא proves each one from a פסוק. The גמרא challenges this with רבי ענני בר ששון's teaching that each of the בגדי כהונה atones for a sin, including the מעיל for לשון הרע. It answers that לשון הרע which caused harm brings נגעים, while harmless לשון הרע is atoned for by the מעיל. A new teaching says the עגלה ערופה atones for murder and the קטרת for לשון הרע, which clashes with the כתונת and the מעיל. The גמרא resolves the murder clash and begins resolving the לשון הרע clash, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Something said before three people is not evil speech
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא rules that repeating something said in front of three people is not לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא says: Anything that was said in front of three people does not count as evil speech if someone repeats it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר רב הונא gives a rule. Once something was said in front of three people, repeating it is not considered לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, telling over something negative about a person is forbidden. This rule creates an exception when the information was already said before a group of three. The reason for the rule comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Evil speech (לשון הרע), meaning harmful talk about another person
In the presence of three people
A matter, a thing that was said

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna [says]:
Any matter that was said
in the presence of three [people]
does not have in it [a problem] of evil speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section with a new rule about the limits of לשון הרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Information already said before three people may be repeated without the prohibition of לשון הרע.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why being said before three people removes the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this rule is true. This short question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule sounds surprising, because the information is still negative. The גמרא wants to know what is special about the number three.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבה בר רב הונא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why something said before three people is not considered לשון הרע.

steps.title: Your friend has a friend
steps.stepSummary: Information said before three people will spread anyway, because everyone tells their friends.
steps.simpleTranslation: Your friend has a friend, and your friend's friend has a friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that information said before three people will spread on its own. Each listener tells a friend, and that friend tells another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once three people heard it, the information is treated as already public. Repeating it does not cause any new harm, so it is not counted as לשון הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: Your friend
Has a friend

steps.whatToRemember: Something said before three people is treated as public knowledge, because everyone has a friend they will tell.

phrases.english: Your friend has a friend,
and your friend's friend has a friend.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Information said before three people will spread anyway, so repeating it is not לשון הרע.

steps.title: What does the פסוק about loud blessing mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי asks what the פסוק in משלי means when it says a loud blessing counts as a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: What does the verse mean, 'He who blesses his friend with a loud voice, rising early in the morning, it will be counted as a curse for him'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי quotes a פסוק that sounds strange: a blessing that turns into a curse. He is setting up his own explanation, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from negative speech to praise. The puzzle is how blessing someone could ever count as cursing him.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
What is the meaning of what is written?
It will be counted as a curse for him

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
What is [the meaning of] what is written:
"He who blesses his friend with a loud voice,
rising early in the morning,
it will be counted as a curse for him"?
phrases.notes: משלי 27:14

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב מְבָרֵךְ רֵעֵהוּ בְּקוֹל גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from harmful speech to the risk of public praise.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a blessing can count as a curse.

steps.title: Praising a generous host brings him trouble
steps.stepSummary: A guest who loudly praises his host in the marketplace causes people to come and take advantage of the host.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, someone stays at a host, and the host takes very good care of him. The next day the guest goes out, sits in the marketplace, and says: 'May God bless so-and-so, who took such care of me!' People hear this, go to the host, and force themselves on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains the פסוק with an example. A guest's loud public praise sends crowds to the host, who now has to look after all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guest meant to bless his host, but his public praise put a heavy burden on him. That is how a loud blessing becomes a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: A host, a place where a guest stays
They went to trouble for him, they looked after him
The marketplace
They pressure him, take advantage of him

phrases.english: For example, when one happens to come to a host
and they go to great trouble for him,
the next day he goes out, sits in the marketplace, and says:
May the Merciful One bless so-and-so
who went to so much trouble for me,
and people hear
and go and take advantage of him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 with a practical case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Public praise of a generous host sends crowds to him, so the blessing turns into a burden.

steps.title: Never speak about another person's goodness
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי the brother of רב ספרא teaches that praising someone leads to speaking badly about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי, the brother of רב ספרא, taught: A person should never talk about the goodness of his friend, because from talking about his goodness he will come to talk about his bad side.
steps.whatsHappening: A teaching is brought that a person should not praise someone else in public. Praise tends to lead to criticism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits with the previous step: praise can backfire. Here the harm is not money but speech, because praise invites someone to add 'but he also has this flaw'.

keyTerms.meaning: One should never tell
About the goodness of his friend
He comes to [speak of] his bad side

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean praising someone is itself לשון הרע. The worry is that praise often leads into criticism.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא:
phrases.english: Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, taught:
A person should never speak
about the goodness of his friend,
because from [speaking of] his goodness
he comes to [speak of] his bad side.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם אַל יְסַפֵּר אָדָם בְּטוֹבָתוֹ שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about the dangers of praise.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not praise another person, because the praise leads to talking about his faults.

steps.title: Another version: רב דימי is sick
steps.stepSummary: A second version tells that רב ספרא visited his sick brother רב דימי, who claimed he had kept everything the חכמים said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב דימי, the brother of רב ספרא, was sick. רב ספרא came in to visit him. רב דימי said to those present: Let merit come to me, since I have kept everything the חכמים said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how this teaching came about. It sets up a story where רב דימי claims he kept every teaching of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב דימי did not teach the rule himself. His boast sets up the challenge from his brother in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Became sick
To ask about his health, to visit him
Let it (merit) come to me

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: רַב דִּימִי אֲחוּהּ דְּרַב סָפְרָא חֲלַשׁ,
phrases.english: Rav Dimi, the brother of Rav Safra, was sick,
Rav Safra went in to ask about his health.
He said to them: Let [merit] come to me,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the sick רב דימי, talking to the people around him.

phrases.english: for I have kept everything the Rabbis said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of where the teaching of step 6 came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב דימי claims he fulfilled all the teachings of the חכמים.

steps.title: רב ספרא challenges: did you keep the rule about praise?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks his brother whether he kept the rule against praising others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to him: Did you keep this one: A person should never speak about the goodness of his friend, because from his goodness he comes to his shame?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא challenges his brother's claim. He brings up a teaching he thinks רב דימי did not keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was that רב דימי kept every rule. One rule he may have missed is enough to challenge it. In this version the rule ends with 'his shame' instead of 'his bad side', but the idea is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Have you kept this one?
His shame, something disgraceful about him

phrases.english: He said to him: Have you kept this one:
A person should never speak
about the goodness of his friend
because from [speaking of] his goodness
he comes to [speak of] his shame?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's claim from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that he kept everything the חכמים said.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One rule he did not keep, the rule against praising others, is enough to disprove 'everything'.

steps.title: I never heard it, but I would have kept it
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that he never heard this teaching, and would have kept it if he had.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I never heard it, and if I had heard it, I would have kept it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי replies that this rule was new to him. Had he known it, he would have kept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer limits his claim to the rules he knew. It also shows that in this version the teaching did not come from רב דימי, since he had never heard it.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it
I would have kept it

steps.whatToRemember: Praise can cause harm too: loud praise can burden a generous host, and praising someone can lead to talking about his faults.

phrases.english: He said to them: I did not hear it,
and if I had heard it, I would have kept it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב דימי responds to רב ספרא's challenge.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He did not know this teaching; his claim covered only what he had heard.

steps.title: Seven sins that bring נגעים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that נגעים come because of seven specific sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: נגעים come because of seven things: לשון הרע, murder, a false oath, forbidden relations, arrogance, stealing, and stinginess.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that lists seven sins that cause נגעים. This list sets up the next few steps, where each sin will be proven from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was mainly about speech and לשון הרע. Now רבי יוחנן widens the picture: לשון הרע is only one of seven sins that bring צרעת. The list is a claim that still needs proof, and the גמרא proves it one item at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Skin marks of צָרַעַת, seen as a punishment for sin
Speaking badly about others
Murder, literally 'spilling blood'
A false or pointless oath
Arrogance, being full of oneself
Stinginess, literally 'narrowness of the eye'

steps.whatToRemember: There are seven sins that bring נגעים: לשון הרע, שפיכות דמים, שבועת שוא, גילוי עריות, גסות הרוח, גזל, and צרות העין.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Leprous marks come for seven things:

phrases.aramaic: עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, וְעַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים,
phrases.english: for malicious speech, and for bloodshed,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא, וְעַל גִּילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת,
phrases.english: and for a vain oath, and for forbidden relations,
and for arrogance, and for theft,
and for stinginess.
phrases.notes: Literally 'narrowness of the eye': someone who can't stand to share what he has.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the stories about praise and לשון הרע to a broader list of sins that cause נגעים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נגעים come as a punishment for seven sins.

steps.title: Source for לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him' proves that לשון הרע brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For לשון הרע, as it says: 'Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will destroy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving the list, beginning with the first sin, לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about someone who speaks against his friend in secret and says 'I will destroy him.' The word אצמית, 'destroy', is read as hinting at צרעת. So speaking badly about others is linked to נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written, introducing a פסוק
One who slanders, speaks against others
In secret, behind someone's back
I will destroy, here hinting at צרעת

phrases.english: For malicious speech, as it is written:
"Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret,
phrases.notes: תהלים 101:5

phrases.english: him I will destroy."
phrases.notes: Earlier the גמרא read this word 'destroy' as a hint to צרעת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first item on רבי יוחנן's list.

steps.title: Source for murder
steps.stepSummary: דוד's curse on the house of יואב, which includes a מצורע, proves that שפיכות דמים brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For murder, as it says about יואב: 'Let the house of יואב never be without a זב and a מצורע.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second sin, murder, from a פסוק about יואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יואב killed אבנר, and דוד cursed his family. One of the punishments in that curse is a מצורע. This shows that murder is punished with צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: A man with an unusual bodily discharge that makes him טמא
A person struck with צרעת
'And so on': the פסוק continues

phrases.english: For bloodshed, as it is written:
"And let there not fail from the house of Joab
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 3:29. דוד says this after יואב killed אבנר.

phrases.english: a zav and a leper, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second item on the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 3:29, the curse on the house of יואב.

steps.title: Source for a false oath
steps.stepSummary: The story of נעמן and גיחזי, which ends with גיחזי getting צרעת, proves that שבועת שוא brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a false oath, as it says: 'And נעמן said: Swear, and take two talents.' And it says: 'The צרעת of נעמן shall cling to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the third sin, a false oath, by putting two פסוקים from the story of גיחזי side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הואל is read as 'swear.' נעמן asked גיחזי to swear that אלישע had sent him for the gift, and גיחזי swore falsely. The second פסוק shows his punishment: נעמן's צרעת stuck to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Here read as 'swear'; usually 'please' or 'agree'
Two talents, large weights of silver
Shall cling, stick to

steps.confusionAlert: The first פסוק does not mention an oath directly. The proof depends on reading הואל as 'swear', and the person who swore falsely and got צרעת was גיחזי, not נעמן.

phrases.english: And for a vain oath, as it is written:
"And Naaman said: Be content, take two talents,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:23. Here הואל is read as 'swear': נעמן asked גיחזי to swear that אלישע had sent him.

phrases.english: and it is written: "The leprosy of Naaman shall cling to you, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 5:27. אלישע says this to גיחזי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third item on the list.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 5:23 and 5:27, the story of נעמן and גיחזי.

steps.title: Forbidden relations bring נגעים: the case of פרעה
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק that says ה׳ struck פרעה with נגעים, when he took שרה, proves that גילוי עריות brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for forbidden relations, as it is written: 'And ה׳ struck פרעה with great afflictions, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the fourth sin on רבי יוחנן's list, גילוי עריות. It points to פרעה, who was struck with נגעים after taking שרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the very word נגעים for פרעה's punishment. The story is about him taking another man's wife, so the גמרא reads the נגעים as a punishment for גילוי עריות.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden sexual relations
And He struck (with נגעים)
Afflictions, skin plagues

phrases.english: And for forbidden relations —
as it is written: 'And the Lord struck Pharaoh'
phrases.notes: בראשית 12:17. This is when פרעה took שרה, אברהם's wife.

phrases.english: with afflictions, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of proofs for רבי יוחנן's seven sins, after the proof for שבועת שוא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 12:17, where ה׳ strikes פרעה with נגעים because of שרה.

steps.title: Arrogance brings נגעים: the case of King עוזיהו
steps.stepSummary: King עוזיהו became arrogant and went to offer קטורת in the בית המקדש, and צרעת broke out on his forehead. This proves that גסות הרוח brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for arrogance, as it is written: 'When he was strong his heart became haughty, until he acted corruptly, and he betrayed ה׳ his God,' and 'the צרעת broke out on his forehead.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the fifth sin, גסות הרוח (arrogance). It joins two פסוקים about King עוזיהו: first he grew proud, then he got צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes the sin: his heart 'grew high' once he became strong. The second פסוק shows the punishment: צרעת on his forehead. Putting them together shows the arrogance caused the צרעת.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrogance, haughtiness
His heart became high, he grew proud
And he betrayed, acted unfaithfully
The skin plague (often called 'leprosy')

phrases.english: And for arrogance — as it is written:
'And when he was strong his heart became haughty'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 26:16, about King עוזיהו.

phrases.english: until he acted corruptly
and he betrayed the Lord his God,'
'and the leprosy broke out on his forehead.'
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 26:19, a few פסוקים later in the same story.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next proof in the list, after גילוי עריות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 26:16 and 26:19, the story of עוזיהו.

steps.title: Theft brings נגעים: the priest empties the house
steps.stepSummary: When a house has a נגע, the כהן orders it emptied. A ברייתא explains: he gathered money that was not his, so the כהן comes and scatters his belongings. This shows that גזל brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for theft, as it is written: 'And the כהן shall command, and they shall empty the house.' It was taught: He gathered money that is not his, so let the כהן come and scatter his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the sixth sin, גזל (theft). It uses the law that a house with a נגע must be emptied, and a ברייתא explains why that fits a thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proof is measure for measure. The thief brought in things that did not belong to him, so his punishment is that his own things get taken out of his house. The emptying of the house matches the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Theft, robbery
And they shall empty out
Gathers in, collects
And will scatter

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק itself does not mention theft. The proof comes from the ברייתא, which explains that emptying the house is a fitting punishment for someone who filled it with stolen things.

phrases.english: And for theft — as it is written:
'And the priest shall command, and they shall empty the house.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:36. This is about a נגע that shows up on a house, not on a person.

phrases.english: It was taught: He gathered money
that is not his,
so let the priest come and scatter his money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next proof in the list, after גסות הרוח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 14:36 (emptying the house), explained by a ברייתא as measure for measure.

steps.title: Stinginess brings נגעים: 'the one whose house is his'
steps.stepSummary: The תורה calls the owner of the house 'the one whose house is his.' דבי רבי ישמעאל explains this means someone who kept his house only for himself. This proves that צרות העין brings נגעים, and it completes all seven sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for stinginess, as it is written: 'And the one whose house it is shall come.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This is someone who keeps his house only for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the seventh and last sin, צרות העין (stinginess). It reads extra meaning into the way the תורה describes the homeowner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have just said 'the owner,' but it says 'the one whose house is his.' The school of רבי ישמעאל reads this as a hint to his sin: he acted as if his house belonged only to him and would not share it with others.

keyTerms.meaning: Stinginess, an unwillingness to share
The one whose house it is
Set aside only for, kept exclusively for

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's seven sins that bring נגעים, each with a source: לשון הרע, שפיכות דמים, שבועת שוא, גילוי עריות (פרעה), גסות הרוח (עוזיהו), גזל (emptying the house), and צרות העין (the house that is 'his').

phrases.english: And for stinginess — as it is written:
'And the one whose house it is shall come,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:35. Literally 'the one to whom the house belongs.'

phrases.english: and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
one whose house is kept only for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final proof in the list, after גזל, completing all seven sins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 14:35, as explained by דבי רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Is that so? The priestly garments atone like offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim that לשון הרע brings נגעים by quoting רבי ענני בר ששון: the בגדי כהונה atone, just like קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רבי ענני בר ששון say: why is the תורה section about the priestly garments placed right next to the section about offerings? To teach that just as offerings bring atonement, the priestly garments also bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against what it just taught. It is setting up a list showing that each priestly garment atones for a specific sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ענני בר ששון learns from the fact that the two Torah sections sit side by side. Since they are next to each other, the garments share the same power as the offerings, which is atonement. This sets up the challenge, because if a garment atones for a sin, a punishment like נגעים might not be needed for that sin.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?', a word that opens a challenge
The special garments worn by the כהנים
Was placed next to (learning from Torah sections that sit side by side)
Offerings brought in the משכן or בית המקדש
They atone, meaning they bring forgiveness for sin

steps.confusionAlert: The 'Is that so?' is not yet clear in this step. The real clash only shows up later in the list, when the מעיל is said to atone for לשון הרע, which is one of the seven sins that bring נגעים.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Anani bar Sason say:
Why was the section of the priestly garments placed next to
the section of offerings?
phrases.notes: The offerings are in ויקרא chapters 1–7, and the garments come right after, in chapter 8.

phrases.english: To tell you:
Just as offerings atone,
so too the priestly garments atone.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי עֲנָנִי בַּר שָׂשׂוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs that the seven sins bring נגעים, the גמרא now questions that list.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim (steps 10–11) that לשון הרע brings נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the בגדי כהונה atone for sins, then those sins are already forgiven, so why would נגעים still come?

steps.title: The tunic and the trousers
steps.stepSummary: The כתונת atones for murder, and the מכנסים atone for forbidden relations. Each is supported by a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tunic atones for bloodshed, because it says that the brothers dipped יוסף's coat in blood. The trousers atone for forbidden relations, because it says they were made to cover nakedness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the garments one by one, beginning with the כתונת and the מכנסים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each garment is linked to a sin through a פסוק. The word כתונת shows up in the story of יוסף's coat being dipped in blood, so it fits murder. The מכנסים cover nakedness, so they fit forbidden relations.

keyTerms.meaning: The tunic worn by the כהן
Bloodshed, murder
The linen trousers of the כהן
Forbidden relations

phrases.english: The tunic atones for bloodshed,
as it is written: 'And they dipped the coat in the blood.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 37:31. This is יוסף's coat.

phrases.english: The trousers atone for forbidden relations,
as it is written: 'And make for them linen trousers
to cover the flesh of nakedness.'
phrases.notes: שמות 28:42

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוֹנֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts filling in the details of רבי ענני בר ששון's teaching that the garments atone.
steps.raayaObject: That the כתונת atones for murder and the מכנסים atone for forbidden relations.

steps.title: The turban and the belt
steps.stepSummary: The מצנפת atones for arrogance, because something high up atones for 'high' behavior. The אבנט atones for sinful thoughts, because it sits over the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The turban atones for arrogant people. As רבי חנינא said: let something that sits up high come and atone for acting 'high'. The belt atones for thoughts of the heart, since it sits right where the heart is, as it says, 'on אהרן's heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with two more garments. This time the links come from where each garment is worn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצנפת is worn on the head, the highest place, so it atones for a person who carries himself 'high', meaning arrogance. The אבנט sits at the area of the heart, so it atones for sins of the heart, meaning thoughts.

keyTerms.meaning: The turban worn on the כהן's head
Arrogant people
Height, used here for both a high place and haughtiness
The belt or sash of the כהן
Thoughts of the heart, sinful thinking

phrases.english: The turban atones for the arrogant,
in line with Rabbi Chanina,
for Rabbi Chanina said:
Let something that sits up high come
and atone for an act of haughtiness.
The belt atones for thoughts of the heart,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, which fits אבנט better. Both mean 'atones'.

phrases.english: for the place where it is,
phrases.notes: He means it atones for sins that happen in the spot where it sits, which is the heart.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And it shall be upon Aaron's heart.'
phrases.notes: שמות 28:30

steps.triggerLanguage: מִצְנֶפֶת מְכַפֶּרֶת עַל גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ — כִּדְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of garments and the sins they atone for.
steps.raayaObject: That the מצנפת atones for arrogance and the אבנט atones for sinful thoughts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חנינא's reasoning about height, and שמות 28:30

steps.title: Breastplate, ephod, and robe: the robe atones for evil speech
steps.stepSummary: The חושן atones for bad judgments, the אפוד atones for idol worship, and the מעיל atones for לשון הרע. That last one clashes with the teaching that לשון הרע brings נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The breastplate atones for judgments, since it is called the 'breastplate of judgment.' The ephod atones for idol worship, since the פסוק pairs 'no ephod' with idols. The robe atones for evil speech. הקב"ה said: let something that makes a sound come and atone for a sin done with sound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists three more garments. The third, the מעיל, is the heart of the challenge, because it atones for לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said לשון הרע brings נגעים. Now we hear that the מעיל already atones for לשון הרע. If the sin is already forgiven through the garment, why would a person still get נגעים? That is what 'איני?' was asking.

keyTerms.meaning: The breastplate of the כהן גדול
The apron-like garment of the כהן גדול
Idols
The robe of the כהן גדול
Evil, hurtful speech about others

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the exact point that clashes with the earlier teaching, so the answer the גמרא gives next must explain how the מעיל and נגעים can both be true.

phrases.english: The breastplate atones for judgments,
phrases.notes: He means judgments that were done wrongly.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And you shall make a breastplate of judgment.'
phrases.notes: שמות 28:15

phrases.english: The ephod atones for idol worship,
as it is written: 'Without ephod or teraphim.'
phrases.notes: הושע 3:4

phrases.english: The robe atones for evil speech,
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let something that makes a sound come
phrases.notes: This is the robe, which had bells on its bottom edge.

phrases.english: and atone for a sin done with the voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list and reaches the garment that creates the actual contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier teaching that לשון הרע brings נגעים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מעיל atones for לשון הרע, so the sin is already forgiven and נגעים should not be needed.

steps.title: The headplate atones for brazenness
steps.stepSummary: The ציץ atones for brazen, shameless behavior. The link is the word מצח (forehead), which appears both in the ציץ's פסוק and in a פסוק about shamelessness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The headplate atones for acts of brazenness. Here it says, 'It shall be on אהרן's forehead,' and there it says, 'You had the forehead of a harlot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list of eight garments with the ציץ. This completes the quote from רבי ענני בר ששון, and the challenge now stands fully built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word, מצח, ties the two פסוקים together. The ציץ sits on the forehead, and a shameless person is described as having a 'harlot's forehead', so the ציץ atones for shamelessness. The next step answers the challenge about the מעיל and לשון הרע.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden headplate of the כהן גדול
Brazen, shameless people
Forehead
'Here it says... and there it says', which links two פסוקים through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ענני בר ששון matches all eight בגדי כהונה to sins. The key one for our סוגיא is that the מעיל atones for לשון הרע, and that clashes with the idea that לשון הרע brings נגעים.

phrases.aramaic: צִיץ מְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עַזֵּי פָנִים —
phrases.english: The headplate atones for acts of brazenness.
Here it is written: 'And it shall be on Aaron's forehead,'
phrases.notes: שמות 28:38

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״וּמֵצַח אִשָּׁה זוֹנָה הָיָה לָךְ״.
phrases.english: and there it is written: 'You had the forehead of a harlot.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 3:3

steps.triggerLanguage: צִיץ מְכַפֵּר עַל מַעֲשֵׂה עַזֵּי פָנִים — כְּתִיב הָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of garments, completing the source quoted in the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That the ציץ atones for brazenness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 28:38 and ירמיהו 3:3, linked by the shared word מצח

steps.title: It depends whether the evil speech actually did damage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the clash between 'לשון הרע brings נגעים' and 'the מעיל atones for לשון הרע' by splitting the cases. If the speech caused harm, נגעים come. If it caused no harm, the מעיל atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It's not a problem. One teaching is about when his words had an effect, and the other is about when they didn't. If his words had an effect, נגעים come on him. If his words had no effect, the מעיל atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 21. It explains that each teaching is talking about a different kind of לשון הרע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two teachings are not arguing; they cover two different cases. When the gossip actually hurt someone or caused a fight, the punishment is נגעים. When the gossip went nowhere, the gentler atonement of the מעיל is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem; the two sources can both be true.
This one ... that one; used to split two sources into two different cases.
His actions had an effect, meaning his words actually caused harm.
The blue robe of the כהן גדול.

steps.whatToRemember: לשון הרע that caused damage brings נגעים. לשון הרע that caused no damage is atoned for by the מעיל.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where his actions had an effect,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the teaching that לשון הרע brings נגעים. 'Had an effect' means his words actually hurt someone.

phrases.english: that is where his actions had no effect.
If his actions had an effect,
leprous marks come upon him;
if his actions had no effect,
the robe atones.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו, הָא דְּלָא אַהֲנוֹ מַעֲשָׂיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 21 between the מעיל and נגעים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two sources cover different situations.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if there were two different consequences for the very same sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Harmful לשון הרע brings נגעים. Harmless לשון הרע is atoned for by the מעיל.

steps.title: A new teaching: murder and evil speech are not atoned for by offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן לוי. Murder and לשון הרע have no atonement through קרבנות, but each has another way of atonement. For murder, it is the עגלה ערופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי סימון say in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: There are two sins that we don't find atoned for by offerings, but we do find something else that atones for them. These are murder and לשון הרע. Murder is atoned for through the עגלה ערופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge by quoting a teaching about what atones for murder and לשון הרע. This step sets up the contradiction that the גמרא will spell out in step 26.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ענני בר ששון said the בגדי כהונה atone, with the כתונת for murder and the מעיל for לשון הרע. Here a different teaching names other things that atone for those same two sins. The first one named is the עגלה ערופה for murder.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'spilling blood'; murder.
The calf whose neck is broken when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown.
Atonement.
Offerings brought in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Simon say
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Two things, we have not found for them
atonement through offerings,
but through something else we have found atonement for them:
bloodshed and evil speech.
Bloodshed is atoned for through the heifer whose neck is broken.
phrases.notes: See דברים 21:1–9.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי סִימוֹן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מעיל question is settled, a new source is brought that will clash with רבי ענני בר ששון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ענני בר ששון's list of what each priestly garment atones for (steps 18–21).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different teaching names other things, the עגלה ערופה and the קטרת, that atone for the same two sins.

steps.title: Incense atones for evil speech
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching continues: לשון הרע is atoned for by the קטרת. This is backed by a ברייתא from רבי חנינא with a פסוק, and by the school of רבי ישמעאל, who explain the connection: both are done in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: And לשון הרע is atoned for through the קטרת. As רבי חנינא taught: We learned that the קטרת atones, as it says, 'He put on the incense and atoned for the people.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: What does the קטרת atone for? For לשון הרע‎. ה׳ said: Let something done in private come and atone for something done in private.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the teaching and proves that the קטרת atones for לשון הרע. It gives a פסוק and a reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק shows that the קטרת can atone at all. The school of רבי ישמעאל then says it atones specifically for לשון הרע. The reason is a measure-for-measure match: the קטרת is burned privately inside the היכל, and לשון הרע is usually spoken quietly behind someone's back.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense burned in the בית המקדש.
Evil speech; saying hurtful things about others.
In private, secretly.

phrases.english: And evil speech is atoned for through incense,
as Rabbi Chanina taught:
We have learned about incense that it atones,
as it is written:
"And he put on the incense and made atonement for the people."
phrases.notes: במדבר 17:12

phrases.english: And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
For what does incense atone?
For evil speech.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Let something done in private come
phrases.notes: The קטרת was burned inside the היכל, away from the people.

phrases.english: and atone for a deed done in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָשׁוֹן הָרָע — בִּקְטֹרֶת, דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי יהושע בן לוי's list and supports its second item.
steps.raayaObject: That the קטרת atones for לשון הרע.
steps.raayaSupportSource: במדבר 17:12 (through רבי חנינא) and the ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Two contradictions laid out side by side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem outright. On murder, the כתונת clashes with the עגלה ערופה. On לשון הרע, the מעיל clashes with the קטרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Murder contradicts murder, and לשון הרע contradicts לשון הרע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names both contradictions between רבי ענני בר ששון and רבי יהושע בן לוי. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sin now has two different things said to atone for it. For murder, it is the כתונת in one source and the עגלה ערופה in the other. For לשון הרע, it is the מעיל in one source and the קטרת in the other. The גמרא needs to explain how both sources can be true.

keyTerms.meaning: One statement is difficult in light of the other; the two sources clash.
The priestly tunic, said in step 19 to atone for murder.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different contradiction from the one answered in step 23. That one was the מעיל versus נגעים. This one is the בגדי כהונה versus the עגלה ערופה and the קטרת.

phrases.english: The teaching on bloodshed contradicts the other teaching on bloodshed,
phrases.notes: The כתונת (step 19) versus the עגלה ערופה (step 24).

phrases.english: and the teaching on evil speech contradicts the other teaching on evil speech!
phrases.notes: The מעיל (step 21) versus the קטרת (step 25).

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים, קַשְׁיָא לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the newly quoted teaching next to רבי ענני בר ששון's list and states the clash.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כתונת atones for murder and the מעיל atones for לשון הרע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources give two different ways of atoning for the same sin, so it is unclear which one is right.

steps.title: Murder: known killer versus unknown killer
steps.stepSummary: The clash between the כתונת and the עגלה ערופה is resolved. The כתונת atones when the killer is known, and the עגלה ערופה atones when the killer is unknown.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two teachings about murder do not clash. One is about a case where we know who killed him, and the other is about a case where we do not know who killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the murder clash from step 26 by saying each source is talking about a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה is only brought when a dead body is found and nobody knows who the killer is. So it covers the unknown-killer case. That leaves the כתונת to atone when the killer is known.

keyTerms.meaning: Bloodshed, meaning murder
It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
This one... that one; used to split two sources into two different cases

phrases.english: Bloodshed against bloodshed
is not difficult:
this is where it is known who killed him,
phrases.notes: "This" is the כתונת, and "that" in the next line is the עגלה ערופה, both from step 26.

phrases.english: that is where it is not known who killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the murder half of the clash raised in step 26
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is placed in a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the כתונת and the עגלה ערופה seemed to be the atonement for the very same sin of murder.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כתונת atones when the killer is known, and the עגלה ערופה atones when the killer is unknown.

steps.title: A known killer should be executed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if we know who the killer is, he deserves the death penalty. How could a garment atone for that?
steps.simpleTranslation: If we know who killed him, that killer deserves to be put to death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave about a known killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A known murderer is put to death by בית דין, and the atonement comes through his punishment. So it seems there is no case of a known killer that is left for the כתונת to atone for.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who deserves the death penalty

phrases.english: Where it is known who killed him,
he deserves to be put to death!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידִיעַ מַאן קַטְלֵיהּ בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the known-killer case set up in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the כתונת atones for a known killer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A known killer is executed, so no case remains where the כתונת would be needed.

steps.title: He killed on purpose but was never warned
steps.stepSummary: The case of a known killer is one where he killed on purpose but nobody warned him first, so בית דין cannot put him to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he killed on purpose, but they did not warn him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a known killer who still cannot be executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית דין can only execute a killer who was warned before the act (התראה). If the killer was known and acted on purpose but got no warning, he goes free from the death penalty. In that case the כתונת is what brings atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose, deliberately
A warning given before a sin; needed before בית דין can punish
They warned him

steps.whatToRemember: For murder: the עגלה ערופה is for an unknown killer. The כתונת is for a known killer who cannot be executed because he was never warned.

phrases.english: Where he did it on purpose, and they did not warn him.
phrases.notes: Without a warning just before the act, בית דין cannot put him to death, even though he did it on purpose.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: a known killer who is exempt from execution
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every known killer is executed, so the כתונת would have nothing to atone for.
steps.terutzMaskana: A killer who acted on purpose without a warning is known but is not executed, and the כתונת atones for him.

steps.title: לשון הרע: the קטרת is for speech said in private
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins resolving the לשון הרע clash. The קטרת atones for לשון הרע spoken in private, and the other half of the split comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two teachings about לשון הרע do not clash. This one is about speech said in private,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the second clash from step 26, between the מעיל and the קטרת, by splitting the cases again. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, the school of רבי ישמעאל linked the קטרת to לשון הרע because both are done in private. So the קטרת is matched to לשון הרע said in private. The case left for the מעיל comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Speaking badly about someone else
Privacy, in secret

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same kind of answer as the murder split in step 27, but here the split is about how the speech was said (in private or not), not about whether the person is known.

phrases.english: Malicious speech against malicious speech
is not difficult:
this is in private,
phrases.notes: "This" is the קטרת, which step 25 tied to things done in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָשׁוֹן הָרָע אַלָּשׁוֹן הָרָע לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the murder half of step 26's clash to the לשון הרע half
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) by how the speech was said
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both the מעיל and the קטרת seemed to atone for the very same sin of לשון הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קטרת atones for לשון הרע said in private. The case for the מעיל comes next.
